description: Each rating's daily rental price is the mean of the per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration.

a.request: For each film rating, work out the average replacement cost and the average per-film daily rental price (divide each film's `rental_rate` by its `rental_duration`, then average these within the rating). Take the simple average of the ratings' daily prices, and keep only the ratings whose daily price is above it. Return a single row with the average of those ratings' average replacement costs, the average of their daily prices, and the average amount by which their daily prices exceed the cross-rating average, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_rc, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS daily FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(daily) AS overall FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_rc) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(r.daily) AS avg_daily_price, AVG(r.daily - m.overall) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.daily > m.overall

c.request: For each film rating, look at its average replacement cost and its rental rate per day of rental duration. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple average across ratings? For those ratings, give one row showing their average replacement cost, their average per-day rate, and on average how far that rate is above the cross-rating average. Don't round. Each rating's daily rental price is the mean of the per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration.
c.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(1.0 * rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_daily_rate FROM film GROUP BY rating), c AS (SELECT AVG(avg_daily_rate) AS cross_avg FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(r.avg_daily_rate) AS avg_daily_rate, AVG(r.avg_daily_rate - c.cross_avg) AS avg_excess_over_cross_rating_avg FROM r CROSS JOIN c WHERE r.avg_daily_rate > c.cross_avg

b.request: Compute each film rating's daily rate as the mean of per-film rental_rate / rental_duration, then take the simple (unweighted) average of those daily rates across the 5 ratings. Keep only ratings whose daily rate exceeds that cross-rating average, and return one row giving the average of their mean replacement_cost, the average of their daily rates, and the average amount by which their daily rates exceed the cross-rating average, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS daily_rate, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_repl FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(daily_rate) AS overall FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_repl) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(r.daily_rate) AS avg_daily_rate, AVG(r.daily_rate - m.overall) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.daily_rate > m.overall

d.request: For each film rating, compute its average replacement cost and its daily rental price, where the daily rental price is the mean of the per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration. Which ratings have a daily rental price above the simple average of the daily rental prices across all ratings? For those ratings, give one row showing their average replacement cost, their average daily rental price, and on average how far their daily rental price is above the cross-rating average. Don't round.
d.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS daily_price FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(daily_price) AS avg_daily FROM per_rating) SELECT AVG(p.avg_replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(p.daily_price) AS avg_daily_rental_price, AVG(p.daily_price - o.avg_daily) AS avg_excess_over_cross_rating_average FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.daily_price > o.avg_daily
